catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-benedict: Benedict X was the antipope the reformers deposed in 1059. This entry traces his intrusion, his condemnation, and his end. The last of the simoniac popes: his deserved fall opened great Hildebrand's age of true Church reform at long last.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-clement-: Clement X was the aged Altieri pope of the early 1670s. This entry notes his pontificate, his charities, and the scant drama of his reign. The octogenarian of the baroque: his generous alms fed the starving Roman poor daily in charity.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-gregory-: Gregory X was the pope of Lyons II and the conclave's iron rules. This entry traces his pontificate, his council, and his reforms. The peacemaker of the long vacancy: his iron conclave rules endure to this very day unchanged in law.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-innocent: Innocent X was the Pamphilj pope of Velázquez's portrait and the Jansenist condemnation. This entry traces his pontificate, his art, and his sternness. The pope of the Doria gallery: his terrible frown frightened the court painters of baroque Rome itself.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-john-x: John X was the pope who crushed the Saracens at Garigliano and fell to Marozia. This entry traces his pontificate, his victory, and his murder. The warrior undone by Rome's harlot: his brutal fall shamed the iron age of Rome.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-leo-x: Leo X was the Medici pope of Luther's revolt and Raphael's Rome. This long entry traces his pontificate, his splendor, and his failure. The pope who lost the north: his fateful indulgences sparked the great German revolt of 1517's autumn.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-pius-x: Pius X was the saintly Sarto pope who warred on Modernism. This entry traces his pontificate, his reforms, and his holiness. The pope of Pascendi: his solemn oath bound the world's clergy against error in 1910's bright September morning forever.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-stephen-: Stephen IX was the Lotharingian reform pope, Frederick of Lorraine. This entry traces his brief pontificate, his reforms, and his death. The reformer of the eleventh century's dawn: his reforming decrees armed young Hildebrand for the coming battle with simony.

doe-osti-3007898-design-and-optimization: IMAGINE-X got designed, and this DOE text optimizes the NB1 diffractometer. The pages detail the findings. The neutron folks get their layout. The instrument was IMAGINE-X. The layout was neutron. The hall was NB1. The instrument was diffractometer.
doe-osti-3013903-surrogate-model-integra: MOOSE XFEM got surrogate-integrated, and this DOE text grows creep cracks by model. The pages detail the findings. The engineers get their method. The growth was creep crack. The method was engineer. The code was MOOSE. The integration was surrogate.
the-duchess-of-berry-and-the-court-of-ch:
Imbert de Saint-Amand's The Duchess of Berry and the Court of Charles X maps the French court from 1824 on. Its contents run from the accession of Charles X, his entry into Paris, and the tombs of Saint-Denis to the coronation at Rheims, the jubilee of 1826, and the ministry of Polignac. Balls, reviews, and trips fill the middle.

At its heart stands Marie Caroline, the widowed Duchess of Berry, gay centre of court life. Saint-Amand writes with a royalist's warmth. The book shows a gay court dancing toward the fall of 1830.
